cards.title: Seed pitch
cards.prompt: Raise a one point five million dollar seed round for a scheduling tool for clinics with forty paying clinics.
strong_answer_covers: The ask and the round size in the first minute
Why now and why this team, in one or two sentences each
Traction with numbers: paying clinics, growth, churn
Market size built bottom up, not a top down headline
Biggest risk named honestly with a plan
Use of funds tied to milestones
Asks for a concrete next step, such as a partner meeting
Answers the churn question directly

cards.title: Pilot proposal
cards.prompt: Sell a six month pilot of route planning software to a regional distributor that plans routes in spreadsheets today.
strong_answer_covers: Leads with the problem in the client's numbers: fuel, overtime, late deliveries
Price framed against savings and payback
Implementation plan that protects drivers and dispatchers
Clear pilot success criteria agreed up front
Asks for a decision and a start date
Shows savings instead of attacking the spreadsheet; holds price unless something is traded

cards.title: Status update with an ask
cards.prompt: Tell the VP the launch is slipping three weeks and ask for one more engineer.
strong_answer_covers: Bottom line first: the slip, the cause, the ask
Options with trade-offs, not just the ask
Who loses the engineer and what that costs
A date with confidence level
Gets an explicit decision
No new bad news surfaces only under probing

cards.title: Offer negotiation
cards.prompt: Negotiate an offer of one hundred and twenty thousand base when market data says one hundred and thirty five.
strong_answer_covers: Expresses enthusiasm and states a specific number with a reason
Uses market data and the competing process without bluffing
Asks about every lever: base, sign on, equity, level, start date
Stays above the walk away point
Agrees concrete next steps and a date
Does not accept the first counter on the spot; never bluffs about an offer

cards.title: Hard performance review
cards.prompt: Tell a strong engineer that missed review deadlines are frustrating the team, and agree a plan.
strong_answer_covers: States the gap early, with specific examples and impact
Separates the person from the behaviour
Listens and acknowledges their view
Agrees a concrete plan with a check in date
Keeps the relationship and their strengths in view
The message stays clear; listens rather than argues

cards.title: Project kickoff
cards.prompt: Kick off an eight week project to rebuild new user onboarding across three teams.
strong_answer_covers: States the goal and the success metric
Scope in and out, explicitly
Named owners for each workstream
Risks and how the timeline accounts for them
Agrees the first milestone and date
Does not accept a doubted date without changing scope or resources
